title: 九歌·国殇
titleEn: Nine Songs: For Those Who Died for the State
author: 屈原
intro: A battlefield hymn from 2,300 years ago, sung to honour soldiers of the state of Chu who died fighting. It moves from the chaos of chariots and arrows to the silent bodies on the plain — and ends by calling them heroes even among ghosts.
analysis: “国殇”指为国家战死的人。《九歌》本是楚国祭神的歌，这一首祭的是阵亡将士。前半写战斗：拿着吴国的戈、穿着犀牛皮的甲，战车车轴相撞，短刀相接；旗子遮住太阳，敌人多得像云，箭像雨一样落下，战士们却争着向前。敌人冲破阵地，战马倒下，战车陷进泥里，主帅还拿起鼓槌击鼓。接着画面突然安静：将士全部战死，尸体留在原野上——“出不入兮往不反”，出征的人再也回不来了。后半是赞歌：他们身首分离，心却不后悔；真是勇敢又有武艺，到死刚强、不可欺负。最后两句是全诗的高潮：身体虽死，精神永存，魂魄也是鬼中的英雄。全诗每句中间用“兮”，节奏急促有力，像战鼓。这首诗是中国最早歌颂为国牺牲的作品之一。
analysisEn: 国殇 means those who died for their country. The Nine Songs were hymns sung at religious rites in the state of Chu, and this one honours fallen soldiers. The first half is the battle itself, told at speed: soldiers grip spears from Wu and wear rhinoceros-hide armour; chariot hubs crash together and men fight hand to hand; banners blot out the sun, enemies swarm like clouds, arrows fall like rain — and still the soldiers race forward. The line breaks, horses fall, wheels sink into the mud, and the commander keeps beating the war drum. Then the noise suddenly stops. Everyone is dead, left lying on the open plain: “they went out and never came in, set off and never returned.” The second half turns into praise. Their heads are cut from their bodies, but their hearts feel no regret; they were brave and skilled, strong to the very end. The closing lines lift the poem: the body has died, but the spirit lives on — even among ghosts, these men are heroes. The 兮 in the middle of every line gives a hard, pounding rhythm, like drumbeats. It is one of the earliest Chinese poems to honour people who died for their country.
background: Qu Yuan (c. 340–278 BC) was a nobleman and minister of the state of Chu who was exiled after his advice was rejected; he is traditionally said to have drowned himself in the Miluo River, which the Dragon Boat Festival remembers. The Nine Songs are traditionally credited to him, reworking Chu’s ritual songs, though some scholars think he only edited them.
pronunciation: 被 pī（同“披”）；毂 gǔ；躐 liè；行 háng（行列）；骖 cān；殪 yì；霾 mái（同“埋”）；絷 zhí；枹 fú（鼓槌）；怼 duì；挟 xié；惩 chéng；为 wéi。机器朗读易错处已在“朗读用字”列替换同音字，音频需人工听验。
version: 采用通行的教材文本（王逸《楚辞章句》系统）。异文：“魂魄毅兮为鬼雄”，王逸本作“子魂魄兮为鬼雄”，通行教材用“魂魄毅兮”；“天时怼兮”一作“天时坠兮”。全诗十八句，网站一行一联（共九行）。

lines.zh: 操吴戈兮被犀甲，车错毂兮短兵接。
lines.rhythm: 操吴戈兮/被犀甲，车错毂兮/短兵接
lines.py: cāo wú gē xī pī xī jiǎ, chē cuò gǔ xī duǎn bīng jiē
lines.lit: Holding Wu spears, wearing rhino armour; chariot hubs clash, short weapons meet.
lines.en: Spears from Wu in hand, rhino-hide on our backs — wheel grinds on wheel, and blade meets blade.
lines.tts: 操吴戈兮披犀甲，车错鼓兮短兵接。

lines.zh: 旌蔽日兮敌若云，矢交坠兮士争先。
lines.rhythm: 旌蔽日兮/敌若云，矢交坠兮/士争先
lines.py: jīng bì rì xī dí ruò yún, shǐ jiāo zhuì xī shì zhēng xiān
lines.lit: Banners hide the sun, the enemy like clouds; arrows cross and fall, soldiers vie to be first.
lines.en: Banners blot out the sun, the enemy thick as clouds; arrows rain down, and our men charge on.

lines.zh: 凌余阵兮躐余行，左骖殪兮右刃伤。
lines.rhythm: 凌余阵兮/躐余行，左骖殪兮/右刃伤
lines.py: líng yú zhèn xī liè yú háng, zuǒ cān yì xī yòu rèn shāng
lines.lit: They overrun our line, trample our ranks; the left horse falls dead, the right is cut by blades.
lines.en: They break through our lines and tread down our ranks; one horse lies dead, the other bleeds.
lines.tts: 凌余阵兮列余航，左餐益兮右刃伤。

lines.zh: 霾两轮兮絷四马，援玉枹兮击鸣鼓。
lines.rhythm: 霾两轮兮/絷四马，援玉枹兮/击鸣鼓
lines.py: mái liǎng lún xī zhí sì mǎ, yuán yù fú xī jī míng gǔ
lines.lit: Two wheels buried, four horses tangled; he grasps the jade drumstick and beats the sounding drum.
lines.en: The wheels sink deep, the horses are caught fast — he seizes the drumstick and beats the drum.
lines.tts: 埋两轮兮直四马，援玉浮兮击鸣鼓。

lines.zh: 天时怼兮威灵怒，严杀尽兮弃原野。
lines.rhythm: 天时怼兮/威灵怒，严杀尽兮/弃原野
lines.py: tiān shí duì xī wēi líng nù, yán shā jìn xī qì yuán yě
lines.lit: Heaven is bitter, the mighty spirits rage; cruelly slain to the last, they are left on the plain.
lines.en: Heaven turns against them, the gods are angry; all are cut down and left on the open field.
lines.tts: 天时对兮威灵怒，严杀尽兮弃原野。

lines.zh: 出不入兮往不反，平原忽兮路超远。
lines.rhythm: 出不入兮/往不反，平原忽兮/路超远
lines.py: chū bù rù xī wǎng bù fǎn, píng yuán hū xī lù chāo yuǎn
lines.lit: They went out and did not come in, went and did not return; the plain is vast, the road endlessly far.
lines.en: They marched out and never came home; the plain stretches empty, the road home is far away.

lines.zh: 带长剑兮挟秦弓，首身离兮心不惩。
lines.rhythm: 带长剑兮/挟秦弓，首身离兮/心不惩
lines.py: dài cháng jiàn xī xié qín gōng, shǒu shēn lí xī xīn bù chéng
lines.lit: Wearing long swords, carrying Qin bows; head and body parted, their hearts do not regret.
lines.en: Long swords at their sides, Qin bows in their arms — heads severed, but their hearts unbroken.

lines.zh: 诚既勇兮又以武，终刚强兮不可凌。
lines.rhythm: 诚既勇兮/又以武，终刚强兮/不可凌
lines.py: chéng jì yǒng xī yòu yǐ wǔ, zhōng gāng qiáng xī bù kě líng
lines.lit: Truly brave, and skilled in arms as well; strong to the end, they could not be humbled.
lines.en: Brave they were, and skilled in war; strong to the very end, no one could shame them.

lines.zh: 身既死兮神以灵，魂魄毅兮为鬼雄。
lines.rhythm: 身既死兮/神以灵，魂魄毅兮/为鬼雄
lines.py: shēn jì sǐ xī shén yǐ líng, hún pò yì xī wéi guǐ xióng
lines.lit: Their bodies dead, their spirits live on; their souls are resolute, heroes among ghosts.
lines.en: Their bodies are gone, but their spirits live — even among the dead, they are heroes.

words.en: those who died for the state
words.note: 殇：未成年而死，也指战死。今天书面语仍用。

words.en: a dagger-axe made in Wu (famous for weapons)
words.note: 戈：古代长柄兵器，今天有“干戈”“倒戈”。
车轮中心的部分，今天不用。
成语“短兵相接”，今天也比喻面对面激烈争论。

words.en: the outer horse of a chariot team

words.note: 通“埋”；今天“雾霾”的“霾”是空气污染。
李清照“死亦为鬼雄”就从这里来。

imagery.name: 剑
imagery.zh: 长剑和秦弓到死都带在身上，象征战士的勇敢和至死不屈。
imagery.en: The long swords they still wear in death stand for courage that never surrendered.

imagery.name: 鼓
imagery.zh: 战车陷住了，主帅还在击鼓：鼓声是不肯放弃的战斗意志。
imagery.en: With the chariot stuck fast, the commander still beats the drum — the will to fight on.

imagery.name: 马
imagery.zh: 左边的马死了、右边的马受伤，写出战斗惨烈。
imagery.en: One horse dead, the other wounded: the brutality of the battle in one image.
